explanations.text:
# INFORMATION

human.json holds:
  human files,
  abstraction paths

a file keeps the lines of the file and every abstraction.
the .json has which piece of the file each abstraction is about.



# WEB LOADS

every five seconds, at the same time:
    the page asks for human.json
    if first time, ask the server once for maps, which holds the abstraction_<name>.json of every file in the map folder. 
    [ask the server for a tip](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:loadTip)

a file with no .json record gets an empty one
a file shows and gets requested only when opened

if tip:
    if tip names a file,
        open that file first.
        a green hand-drawn font arrow with "This is human code" floats at the right of the first line of the draft.
    if tip points at a line of an abstraction:
        abstraction opens and the page scrolls the line to a third of the screen.
        light it with a slow yellow glow; 
        a green hand-drawn arrow with "This is a new change" floats up and down at the right of the line;    
    the green compile button glows 
if click away or compiled, the tip goes away.

[every three seconds](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:pollQueue):
    web asks the server which watch events still wait
    if AI harness runs human ack <event>:
        stop showing message
        read the map of that file again


for each one: 
  the page reads its .json record, human_<name>.json, from maps

then it joins the list at that place, under its own name, <name>.human, at the root when it has no place.
the record it reads and writes stays human/human_<name>.json

the web asks for maps again only when a new file is in the list, and the files it already holds stay as they are,
  the tree shows the new list,
  the file you read stays open, 
  or the first file opens when yours is gone.


# READ

if human serve ran, start the reader from anywhere in the project.

cli climbs to the folder that holds human/human.json and gives it to the one human server of the machine:
  a project with no id in human/human.json stops the run, with the reason.
  if a human server already runs on the port, [the project is handed to it](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:give the server the project) and no second server starts; else it starts one.
  a project is handed over from this machine only.
  each project answers under its own id: http://localhost:<port>/<project id>/human/web.html, so one server serves many projects.
  the server [keeps the list of projects](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:read the list of projects) in ~/.human/projects.json; an id it does not know gets no project.
  when the server takes a project, and on the first ask for it, it brings the old maps up to date: a map named explanation_ becomes abstraction_, and an old human/project.json with words becomes a human file named after the project folder.
  the reader comes inside the human program and [is kept in ~/.human](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:from ~/.human/web.html), not in human/ of the project.
  printing the localhost line and [if not windows, bind tailnet](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:cmd_serve) and [print the tailnet line](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:print_links).
  a port held by another program, or by an older human server, stops the run and says so.

human init starts the reader too, on its --port: it hands the project to the server that runs, or starts one in the background that writes to human/server/serve.log, and prints the same lines.
  a server that does not answer in about ten seconds stops the run and names that log.
  if the project has no human file yet, human init makes the first one, named after the project folder, and prints its name.

keeps open the conection for the next ask and closes it after 30 seconds with no ask.
  if the browser allows it, sends file info compressed 
     
cli answers human.json with a live file list:
  a deleted file leaves the tree and a new one appears, no init, no restart.
  [human init](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:human init) deletes the map in human/ of a file that is not on disk.
  it keeps the list of files on memorychecks only folders with stamp changed.
  the list carries a version code; the web sends back the code it holds.

  if list didn't change, cli answers no chage. else, answers the whole list.

  a file that did not change since the copy the browser holds gets no chage too, and the browser shows its own copy.
  if the new list comes empty, the page keeps the files it shows.


ai harness leaves a tip for the user's first use: human tip <name> --entry <id> --words <words of one line> --say <words>, kept in human/server/tip.json.
  with --add <new line> --after <words of one line>, the new line goes in a draft of the entry under that line, not compiled, and the tip is on the new line.
  with --draft <words> on a human file or an empty map, the words are kept as a draft that is not compiled, and the human file is made when it does not exist.
  words not found inside one line of the entry, an empty --add, an entry the map does not hold, or a draft on a map that holds an abstraction stops the run.
  human tip --clear takes the tip away.

user opens [the reader](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html): 
  cli sends every map file info in one answer:
    reads the maps .json in human/, reads the file path in each .json, ignores maps with no files and maps that are not good JSON.
    tree doesnt' show human/ folder



# EDITOR ON READER

if create file:
  the box opens empty and holds the folder of the row out of sight, so you type the name alone and it lands in that folder; 
    a name that starts with / lands at the root
  [the server makes the file empty](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the new file), so it opens on its new abstraction.
  the code comes under your words. 
if create human:
  refuse if bare name is already held by another human file or a file at the root
  the folder you right-clicked is kept in the map, so the name stands in the tree under that folder as <name>.human, while its record stays human/human_<name>.json.
  the map opens on its new abstraction with no file under it.
no event is queued.
a path out of the project, into human/, or onto a file already there is refused, with the reason. 
the tree follows the files on disk.
git holds no old copy of a file made here,so its first sync runs against an empty old version.
  
cli, it runs human undo <name> --entry <id>, and [the gate refuses it](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the gate)
           while another abstraction stands on that abstraction.
           [The training store](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the training store) and its open session take no part in the undo any more.
  
  
server takes request [as JSON](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:as JSON) —
           and [runs the command you would have typed](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:the command run), one per changed text,
           with the built human program itself, or with human through python:
           an entry rewritten goes in as human retext <name> <id> --verbatim, a first telling as
           human map <name> --verbatim, and code on a file with no map is written to the file.
           A map that holds no entries counts as no map here.
           An expansion you wrote words for goes in the same way, as human map <name> --verbatim, so the
           map holds your words before claude works; an expansion with no words, a decompile and a
           create map nothing at the click — the event alone waits.
           A file under human/ is refused — the maps take no writing.
           The gates are the ones of flow 1: a refusal comes back to the page in the command's own
           words, named by the file and the place it came from, and nothing is queued.

one event appended to human/server/events.jsonl: the kind, the name, the paths of the map and
           the file, the entry, the old text and the new, and for a code write
           [the pins that reach the file](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:the pins that reach a file).
           An expansion and a create name the entry they stand on, and an expansion carries the
           highlighted words with their pins.

user arms the listening once, from the project root: human watch, with no pipeline to filter.

cli [prints every event claude has not finished](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:cmd_watch), one JSON line each, then
           follows the queue; --once prints what waits now and returns. An event printed in an earlier
           session comes back marked replay, so claude reads the maps before it syncs anything.

ai harness takes them in order, by [the writing part of the human skill](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:The reader writes):
           reads the diff of your words, writes the code they ask for — in a new file when no file of the
           project holds that thing —, removes the code they no longer ask for, syncs every map that stood on
           them with --for, so your words follow the code and no word of them changes, and pins the new sentences back in. A decompile, a create, or an expansion with no
           words has no text of yours to read: claude writes that telling itself, in the shape the catalog gives the file, and maps it.
           Then [human ack <number>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:cmd_ack) — the queue
           advances and says how many are left.



# SYNCRONIZATION

if code changes,
    human sync <name>
    a folder in the place of the name is refused.
  
cli runs [a deterministic pass](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:cmd_sync):
  [maps every old line to its new line](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the line map),
  [re-resolves every pin and every span](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the re-resolving).
  if only lines moved, return.
cli finds the abstractions the change touches: lines changed, a pin broken, new lines inside the block.
if the user wrote the words first and the code was written for them: human sync <name> --for <id>. that abstraction [leaves the list](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the entry that leaves): its spans and pins follow the code and no word changes, unless its block is gone. an id no abstraction carries stops the run. a stale repair takes no --for.
cli writes instruction to ai compiler: 
  the file and its absolute path — read the whole file —, 
  the diff,
  [the project files it imports](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the line about the neighbours),
  the blocks,
  the abstractions to mend,
  the rules:
    keep the untouched lines, 
    keep every anchor, 
    add a sentence for each behaviour the change added.
    an abstraction of your own words goes in [named as yours](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the mark on your words),
    find the smallest edit, in the user's voice.

ai compiler [answers with the mended texts](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:ask_claude), 
runs at the project root,
runs claude opus 5.5 at medium effort,
the instruction given through the pipe and never on the command line, so a long one is not cut short.
if claude fails, cli stops and says the reason claude gave.

cli [gates the answer on a copy](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the rebuild), 
tries up to --tries times. checks if: 
  every block exists,
  every anchor kept, 
  every needed word alive. 
  four failures leave the map untouched.
  
the map gets saved; 
the abstractions that point into a mended one get marked stale:
  in the file's map,
  in every map with no code under it, when one of its abstractions pins the mended one if a word changed, and not if the pins alone moved.
           
shows warning:
  if [new lines landed inside an abstraction](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the pieces the new lines fall in) and no word changed.
  if [the sync moved words of your own](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the word when your words moved):
the first copy stays in the map, human show marks the entry with [the line that brings them back](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the word about your words).

if user wants to sync the whole project or a human file, [human sync <bare name>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:cmd_sync). which uses the old state: git HEAD;

cli asks git for [the files that changed](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:changed_files),
re-resolves the file, block, and abstraction pins, and names each one that broke,
[sends one instruction](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:cmd_sync) for the abstraction that pin a changed file.
the diff holds only the changed files those abstractions pin. a file git does not hold yet has no old copy: the diff shows only the lines the pins reach, as new lines.
           
a human file abstraction with the user words goes in named as the users' there too.
the same warning follows when the answer moved them.
--for is taken here too: the abstraction it names leaves the list unless one of its pins broke, its pins follow the code and its words stay. an id no abstraction carries stops the run, and --for with --stale is refused.



## A PARENT ABSTRACTION CHANGED

if sync changed abstraction 1 and other abstractions point to it:
    each abstraction gets [marked as stale](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:mark_children)
    each add to the stale note list of abstraction 1.
    each's copy of the old text gets added to its .json file.
    if other abstraction already stale, keeps its first old text.
    if other abstraction retexts, keep the stale mark


if human sync <name> --stale <id>
    repair and mark gets off. 


cli writes the second letter: one page for each changed parent.
  its old text, 
  its new text, 
  the diff between the two
  then the dependent's text,
  the rules: mend the words that went wrong, 
  keep every anchor and [every word another entry needs](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:needed_words),
  carry a new fact down at the dependent's own level, pinned at the parent's new anchor.
if the dependent holds the user's words, the letter asks for the smallest edit, in the user's voice.
a parent that is gone stops the run.

ai harness answers with the mended dependent. words only, never code.

cli [gates and saves](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:repair_stale); 
marks the dependents of entry 2 as stale in turn.
a repair that moved words of your own is named on the spot, as a sync's is.
a parent's child can be a parent: the next abstraction layer waits for the users next word, one layer at a time. the layers cross maps too. a human file can be the parent of a human file. the chain never turns back on itself.
a human file abstraction made stale by a file's abstraction is repaired the same way:
    each note naming the map and the abstraction it waits on, with the parent read from that map: [human sync <human file> --stale](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:repair_stale).

anchors.words: ask the server for a tip
the project is handed to it
the server makes the file empty
runs the command you would have typed
the pins that reach the file
anchors.anchor: the pins that reach a file

anchors.words: prints every event claude has not finished
the writing part of the human skill
maps every old line to its new line
re-resolves every pin and every span
gates the answer on a copy
new lines landed inside an abstraction
anchors.anchor: the pieces the new lines fall in

anchors.words: the sync moved words of your own
anchors.anchor: the word when your words moved

anchors.words: the line that brings them back

[# THE FILE TREE](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:main)
on the left: the project name and its files.
  a file that holds a writing which is not compiled shows small yellow dot at the left of its row. the dot goes out when the compile passes.
a left click on a file opens that file.
if a right click on the files, a folder or empty space:
  opens a list with two options: "create file" and "create human".
  if any option is clicked:
    a box opens for a name under the folder the right click it's from.
    the grey words say where the name will land, like <path>/<name>
    a name that starts with / drops the folder and lands at the root.

    if empty space, the box stands on the last row of the tree, and that row gives the folder: the root, or the folder it stands in.
    enter [asks the server to make that file inside that folder](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:makeNamed)
    if human:
      the box takes the bare name 
      the folder is the place it shows in 
      it makes a human file, an abstraction with no code under it. 
  pressing escape or clicking anywhere closes the box or the list.

if the server refuses, show warning on top of the reader: 
if pass, only opens the new file and marks it in the tree


[# USER OPENS FILE](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:open)
a file keeps the lines of the file and every abstraction.
the .json has which piece of the file each abstraction is about.

if open: 
  if for the first time, file opens at the header of the abstraction that starts open.
  the page puts the abstractions [in order](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:sorted)
  a pin points from one abstraction at another. 
  the abstraction nobody points at is the most abstract, and it goes last. 
  an abstraction that a pin points at goes above the one that holds the pin, and so on upward. among equals, the one about earlier lines goes first.

if user comes back to a file, the abstractions left open stay open as you left it, and the page stands where you had scrolled it. 
a writing box left open closes when user goes to another file.


[# THE WEB DRAWS THE LIST](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:render)
draws an abstraction as one header line:
  a small arrow, 
  the name of its piece
  its lines. 
if file opened for the first time, [the first of the top layer of abstractions](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:topOf) start open. all others start folded the first time.
under the header the words are drawn exactly as written.

a pin whose target has an abstraction is lit; 
a pin with none is muted; 
a pin the map does not hold yet, one you just typed, is [read from the target it names](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:guessAnchor). 

the bar on top says how many are open.
only as soon as anything differs from the map:
  the word "unsaved", [a compile button](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:header) shows in the page.
  and a dot on that file's row, which even if file is closed, shows.

if the tip points at words in an open abstraction of this file:
  the line with those words glows yellow,
  under the abstraction a note shows the tip and "got it".
if the tip is about compile, [on this file](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:showTip):
  the compile button glows green,
  a note under it shows the tip and "got it".
if any tip of this file also asks for compile, the compile button glows green too, with no note under it.
  and at the right of the glowing line, a green hand drawn arrow points at it and says "This is a new change", floating up and down.
a click on "got it" [ends the tip](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:endTip), and the server forgets it.
 

# NEW ABSTRACTION POSITIONS

the position of the abstraction words you expand on stands on top of the list while the ask is open; 
if file with no map:
  shows one place for a new abstraction and the code of the file under it, 
  the bar says there is no abstraction yet, in the place of the count, with the compiling mark beside it. 
if human file:
  show the abstractions alone, because they have no code. 

an abstraction whose writing waits for the ai harness is marked compiling, with a count when more than one waits. 
a redraw of the same file keeps the page where you had scrolled it, so the words stay under your eyes. 
the head line of an abstraction you asked to take away holds that ask in the place of its name until you send it or drop it.


[# USER WRITES](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:startEdit)
if click on the words:
  a box is put in their place,
  the caret is where user clicked. 

a muted pin shows a name beside its words, and that name counts too
a pin holds the text as it is in the map:
  the pins in their brackets, the targets visible or the code of the file, or nothing for a new abstraction. 

if more text is typed than the size of the box:
  the box grows until its last line shows whole, also when a line wider than the screen gives it a sideways scroll bar.
  if box grow is less than the size of the screen, grow to the bottom of screen.
  the page stays where you scrolled it. 

if escape presed, or user clicks away:
  [the box closes](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:leaveEdit) 
  the text written is kept

[if tab pressed on the box](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:indent):
  four spaces are typed where the caret is
  if lines are selected:
    each line moves four spaces right
  if shift + tab, move the line, or each selected line, four spaces left.
  box stays open

the green circle stays until [ctrl-S or tap on it keeps it on the server](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:save), in human/server/
human code stay in the place written. if the page draws again between one box and the next, same.
only the box now open answers a click away; an older box the page left behind closes nothing.



●  you ask ai harness for an abstraction                  ([the menu](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:menuAt))
│     A right click opens a small menu where you point. On the header
│     of an abstraction it offers [a wider one above it](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:create) and
│     [to take that one away](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:deleteOpen); the ask to take away stands
│     on the head line itself, a click on its name [sends it](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:deleteSend),
│     and cancel, or escape, [lets it go](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:deleteClose). On
│     [words you picked](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:selectedRaw), in the text or in the open box,
│     it offers to expand on them: [a place opens on top of the
│     list](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:expandOpen) where you may add your own words, or none, a
│     click on its name [sends the ask](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:expandSend), and cancel
│     [drops it](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:expandClose). A file with no abstraction yet and some
│     code in it carries decompile over its writing place, which asks
│     for [the whole file to be read and told](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:decompile); an empty
│     file calls that place new abstraction, and a human file, which
│     has no code, calls it that too. Each of these [goes to the
│     server](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:ask) like a compile and comes back as a writing that
│     waits for claude.
│

[#  USER PRESSES COMPILE AND SERVER ANSWERS](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:compile)

save sends the updated abstraction. 
while page waits for server:
  no words show on top
  the compile button turns faint and takes no press

if refusal, show;
  server's refusal, 
  the file it came from in the warning colour, 
  and abstraction stays on web. 

if pass:
  delete the draft, end the tip of that file, redraw the page with [the map again](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:reloadMap)


●  the page watches the queue                         ([pollQueue](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:pollQueue))
│     Every three seconds it asks the server what still waits and
│     marks the entries. When claude finishes, the mark goes, and the
│     page reads the map of that file again, so the new words show.
│
●  you click                                                ([jump](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:jump))
│     A click on a header folds or unfolds that abstraction.
│     A click on a lit pin scrolls to the abstraction it points at,
│     unfolds it, and lights it for a moment; it opens no box.
│

[#  USER JUMPS TO ANOTHER FILE](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:crossJump)

if pin clicked, 
  open that file and goes to the piece the pin names. 
  if pin points to file the project does not hold, show muted and the piece name.
  if the file has no map:
    open the file, go to the lines of that file and lights them for a moment.

  if pin points to one abstraction of that file and words inside it: 
    a click opens the file, 
    goes to that abstraction,
    lights those words for a moment. 

    such a pin to words the abstraction does not hold is muted and shows the file and the number of the abstraction (explain this line?)
  
  [save](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:keepPlace):
    place of the abstraction or file left.
    the file, the abstractions open it it, scroll position.

if back button of the browser, alt and left, the back button of the mouse, or a swipe back on a phone, pressed: [returns to the previous place kept](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:goPlace).
if forward button, or alt and right pressed, return to the next place kept.
in both cases, if writing box left open, it closes when you go back

# FLAGS
map and retext: --verbatim; 
undo: --entry; 
sync: --for;
watch: --once,

tip: --add <new line> --after <words of a line in the entry>, puts the new line in a draft of the entry under that line and the tip asks to compile it;


# COMMANDS

[human init](cmd_init):
    creates the human folder in the project.
    create human/human.json with the list of the project's files.
    
    if none yet, human/human.json gets a short random name as an id
    prints the id and the count of files.
    
    [sweep](scan_files) the project folder and its code files
    drop hidden files, 
    build folders, 
    if folders with a map of their own then pass through [the sieve](is_ignored)
    fill the ignore list of human.json
    add human files to human.json, each with the folder it shows in
    
    a map with the old name explanation_ gets the new name abstraction_, and an old human/project.json with words becomes a human file named after the project folder.
    if the project has no human file yet, make the first human file, named after the project folder, and print its name.
    for each file that is not on disk: delete the its map in human/
    
    if a file at the top of the folder answers to the bare name of a human file:
        show warning that the file needs a new path to be told apart.

    [runs human serve](serve_away)

    

[human serve](cmd_serve):
    finds the top of the project
    if server already runs, [give the server the project](hand_over), [print the reader's link](print_links), stop
    else: 
        start a server in port 8010 unless you say --port <number>
        if new project, create .human in /human/ with project id, [create project id in ~/.human/projects.json](add_project)
    
    [read the list of projects](read_projects) in ~/.human/projects.json. 
    [find project](project_root) by: /<project id>/ 
    
    print:
        "Click <localhost address> to read your human code!"
        if machine has tailnet, print "This is the tailnet <[tailnet address](tailnet_ip)> in case you need it : )", 
    
    [the server running on port <number>](FreshHandler), serves:
        /<project>/..., a file of that project as it is on disk
        /<project>/human/web.html [from ~/.human/web.html](deploy_reader)
        /human/human.json, [rebuilt](fresh_map) on every request
        /human/server/queue, the updates that are not worked yet by the ai harness.
        /human/server/drafts, drafts kept for the project, from human/server/drafts.json.
    
    the server takes [as JSON](read_body):
        1. a writing from the reader             — your own words on an entry, a first
                                              telling for a file with no map, or the
                                              code of that file; the desk hands it to
                                              [the queue](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:compile_writing),
                                              which runs the command you would have
                                              typed and keeps the writing for claude.
                                              When the writing grows a few words of an
                                              entry, the desk passes those marked words
                                              along with it, so the queue knows which
                                              part to grow
        2. a new file from the reader            ([the new file](new_file)) — you name a
                                              path from the top of the project; the
                                              desk makes the file there, empty, and
                                              puts it in the list of the book, so it
                                              waits for its telling. A path that leaves
                                              the project, goes into the human folder,
                                              a hidden or build folder, or a project of
                                              its own, a name with a dot in front, a
                                              suffix the list does not know, a path the
                                              ignore list drops, or a file that is
                                              already there is refused, with the reason

        3. if a new human file from the reader:
            one bare word, no folder and no suffix,
            [the folder](human_place) you made it in, which the map keeps as its place; 
            the desk opens an empty map under that name, for words that stand on no code. 
            a name with a folder, a suffix or a dot in front, 
            a name another human file holds, or a name a file at the root holds is refused, with the reason. 
            a folder is dropped if it leaves the project to go to:
            the human folder, 
            a hidden or build folder, 
            or not on disk
            the map stands at the top

        4. if web draft:
            file path and abstraction
            server writes human/server/drafts.json
            if draft is empy or same draft as the map, remove

        5. Any other writing gets "not found". Every answer
            carries "do not keep me" ([the note](end_headers)), so a
            reload never shows an old copy, and the desk stays quiet
            unless you add --log ([the mute](log_message)).

[human map file --verbatim](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py)
  an abstraction the user sends.
  if --verbatim yes, mark as verbatim.
  the name is a file or a human file by its bare name.
  a folder is refused: a folder has no map.
  the desk hands the whole line to the map run
  [the guard](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py) there keeps the words as you wrote them — they go in plain. 
  a pin in the abstraction is refused.

human retext, undo, show, lines, sync <file>       ([the engine](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py))
    All the work on a map that exists. The desk only points
    the way. retext takes --verbatim too, to put words of your
    own in the place of the ones already mapped. undo takes
    --entry, the number of the entry to drop; without it the
    last entry written goes. sync takes --for, the number of
    the entry the code change was written for: that entry keeps
    its words and only its spans and pins follow. A stale
    repair takes no --for.
    A folder in the place of the file is refused.

human retext, undo, show, lines, sync <human file> ([the project hand](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py))
    The same commands with the bare name of a human file where
    the file goes: the desk sends them to the hand that works on
    the maps of human files, before the engine sees them.

[human watch / human ack <number>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py)
    print every abstraction event ai harness has not compiled, one line each
    each event stays at a queue for the next print; 
    if --once, print and returns.
    if ack <number>, 
        mark the abstraction as compiled and says
        show many abstraction still wait for compilation

[human skills](cmd_skills)
    copy the skill folders, 
    save to ai harnesses skill folders
